reviewStandard: Current identity, rank, and NCBI Taxonomy identifiers were checked against NCBI Taxonomy and current nomenclatural authorities, with conservative appearance bounded by primary descriptions, monographic revisions, or referenced type-strain records. Clostridiales was withheld because Eubacteriales is the current correct order name for NCBITaxon:186802; control subsequently retired the synonym route as an audited asset-free 308 alias to uncovered eubacteriales, and no raster was generated, fabricated, or rekeyed for that transition. Exactly one built-in generation call was made for each of the five supported current subjects using the immutable passive prompt record. The WikiBiome media task and control root inspected every copied PNG at original 1536 by 1024 resolution and reconciled visible bodies, structures, and spatial groupings without trusting prompt counts. Control accepted all five exact originals unchanged, including the honestly recorded Candidozyma prompt-count mismatch. Only those five originals were promoted after approved review-log records and all release gates were established.

assets.scientificFinding: NCBI Taxonomy records Candidozyma auris as current species NCBITaxon:498019 and Candida auris as its basionym. The current combination is MycoBank MB 848169. The original type description supports ovoid, ellipsoidal to elongate budding cells occurring singly, in pairs, or groups and reports no pseudohyphae. This conservative plate is non-diagnostic, and no obsolete-name raster was reused or rekeyed.
assets.visualReview: Exactly nine yeast bodies appear in eight separated groupings: seven isolated smooth ovoid-to-ellipsoidal singles and one touching mother-and-bud pair. This is one more single body and one more grouping than the prompt requested. No pseudohypha, hypha, branching, colony plate, host material, labels, text, scale bar, scenery, clipping, or watermark is visible.

assets.scientificFinding: NCBI Taxonomy recognizes Cladosporium as current genus NCBITaxon:5498. This selected two-structure plate is representative, non-exhaustive, and not genus-diagnostic.
